newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sees economy picking up in coming quarters.
newsitem.headline: Manila sees economy picking up in coming quarters.

text.p: The Philippine economy is expected to pick up steam in coming months despite a slowdown in the manufacturing sector earlier in the year, socioeconomic planning secretary Cielito Habito said on Wednesday.
He said first quarter gross national product (GNP) growth would be about the same as last year's 6.6 percent, and growth rates in the succeeding quarters would be even stronger.
"The GNP (for the first quarter) would be in the neighbourhood of 6-7 percent," Habito told reporters.
"We expect our second and third quarters to be even better than the first quarter, so much so that we are confident of the seven to eight percent target for the full year," he added.
Habito said the manufacturing sector was slowly recovering from a slump. He added that the agriculture and service sectors would more than compensate for the slack in one sector.
A recent Reuter poll of seven brokerages showed that they expected the full-year GNP to fall short of the government's target. Average projections reached only 6.97 percent.

Habito said the manufacturing sector was in a transitory period as companies shifted to high-end products after failing to compete with cheap goods produced by other Southeast Asian countries and China.
Despite the slowdown, the unemployment rate improved to 7.7 percent in January this year from 8.3 percent in the same period last year.
He said most of the new jobs were created by the industrial and service sectors.
The country's chief economic planner reiterated the economy was on track despite the trade and current account deficits.

"It should be noted that much of our imports growth is driven by the recent deregulation of the oil industry as well as the continuing expansion of our production sector," he said in a report to President Fidel Ramos.
